rites.name: Ilyamwen
rites.text: Ilyamwen is a concept of Kroukagar, the sounding that moves through the forming roots of the world during the Holy Age of flame and temple-orders. It is a thread of pitch that binds loose matter into stone and soil, sung rather than seen. Its force is modest and steady, never breaking what it helps to grow.

rites.name: Oseizeth
rites.text: Oseizeth is the sounding of the Singing, the note that holds the first roots of Kroukagar together as they condense from the drifting deep. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, it was the thread that stitched the broken shores back into one resonance.

rites.name: Tania
rites.text: A ritual formula that activates whenever a gatherer picks a fibrous fruit-bearing plant, placing its harvest into the gatherer's satchel.

rites.name: Tesastor
rites.text: A quiet rite that stirs whenever a wanderer gathers a thorn-blossom from the hedgerow, tucking the bloom into their satchel. The gathering alone sets the ritual working.

rites.name: Valontus
rites.text: A keen instinct granted only to the great clawed beasts of the wastes, letting them sense the nearness of fatal harm. It is an innate gift known to no other kind of creature.

rites.name: Raurium Ronauntium
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wanderer endure and resist the poisons of serpents and similar venomous creatures. It is passed along among hardy travelers of the sun-scorched wastes.

rites.name: Vanamanira
rites.text: Vanamanira is a concept of Kroukagar set in the Courts, the age when trials were judged by councils and the doors between worlds were first raised. It embodies the deliberation that decided which thresholds would be built and which left sealed. Its influence is measured in the careful measure of its judgements rather than in raw force.

rites.name: Lontes
rites.text: Lontes is a concept of Kroukagar, the principle that a trial is only binding once it has been witnessed by the council of the Courts. Its adherents hold that a door between worlds opens only when the sworn can name the cost aloud, and they carry this measure into the temples of the Holy Age.

rites.name: Telentum
rites.text: A rare, reserved blessing that cannot be chosen like ordinary talents. It is granted only to one who drinks an enormous quantity of a bitter tonic and carries a favorable fortune.

rites.name: Amostia
rites.text: This charm records whether a band of street raiders has been wiped out. It then steers a sworn vigil task toward its next stage based on that outcome.

rites.name: Sereonia
rites.text: A trained technique that lets a fighter deal extra damage when striking with bare limbs. It is recognized across several branching disciplines of combat.

rites.name: Telonium Oreoses
rites.text: A craft of cloaking things from sight through dappled hues, borrowed light, or cunning forms that pass as something else. Bands of warriors often adopt its patterns to vanish into their surroundings.

rites.name: Tauntonia
rites.text: A discarded talent that once let a wanderer sense the remains of the fallen. The craft was dropped before it ever reached the wider world.

rites.name: Serelleores
rites.text: A written formula for a mixture meant to drive wild beasts away. It is recorded among the miscellaneous items kept in the Library's archive.

rites.name: Nenum
rites.text: A hidden trigger that makes a guardian speak to the wanderer if they leave the sanctuary carrying a young child, provided the guardian still lives.

rites.name: Reoliasum
rites.text: A sacred trigger that stirs when a seeker crosses into its sanctum, advancing a sealed rite and rekindling a visionary mist if it has faded. It only responds while its ritual is still underway.

rites.name: Valiarestes
rites.text: A solemn chant composed by an old master of strings, performed at a hidden shrine. It is sung in the halls of a remote waystation.

rites.name: Tiarnes Cines
rites.text: A learned discipline of close-quarters striking that a wielder cultivates to grow more skilled with blades and blunt weapons. Its practice works like a lasting inherited gift rather than a single act.

rites.name: Seores Valauntum
rites.text: A bodily gift of sharpened sight that lets its holder see clearly through darkness. It is counted among the abilities a person can be granted or earn.

rites.name: Sisanum Amallium
rites.text: A ritual working that purges toxic afflictions from a bearer when it is invoked. It answers many kinds of venom and corruption alike.

rites.name: Viarontor
rites.text: A carved ritual script that applies a flickering ember glow to a restless spirit creature during a coming-of-age trial in a canyon. It shapes how the spirit appears to those who witness the rite.

rites.name: Ristes Orosus
rites.text: A discipline of guardianship that a warrior can learn to strengthen their protective stance. It is taught as one of the lesser arts within a wider training tradition.

rites.name: Teleosolia
rites.text: A learned talent passed on by a keeper of wilderness knowledge, granted as a reward for finishing a trail-craft lesson. It offers several different benefits to those who earn it.

rites.name: Rarnes Miallia
rites.text: A learned skill that lets a fighter strike accurately from farther away than usual. It is a known talent in the tradition of ranged combat.

rites.name: Teleraurnes
rites.text: A one-time signal that wakes a burrowing beast when a traveler crosses a marked threshold. It prompts the creature to abandon its lair and begin hunting or patrolling outward.

rites.name: Elaerennae
rites.text: Elaerennae is the Seeding in Kroukagar, the quiet hour when the makers press the Weave into the soil and the sleeping powers of the grounded realm are lulled back into dormancy. Few beings witness it, and those who do describe a hush that settles over the fields like snow. It is remembered as the moment the world was made gentle.

rites.name: Keloren
rites.text: Keloren is the quiet hour in Kroukagar when the makers press the Weave into the soil and the sleeping powers of the grounded realm settle into stillness. Its effect is subtle, a slow hush rather than a blast, felt most by those who work the land at dusk.

rites.name: Telostiasor
rites.text: A learned knack that grants the bearer an extra quick step in each turn of battle. It is a skill passed among fighters who value swift repositioning.

rites.name: Nallanum
rites.text: A learned fighting art that lets a warrior strike more often with bare hands and blunt grapples. It appears in the battle crafts of several old regions.

rites.name: Meostanes
rites.text: A keen-sighted talent that belongs to the scarred, long-lived folk of the wastes. It sharpens the perception of those who carry it.

rites.name: Rarnistia
rites.text: A quiet hidden rite binds a watcher to a sealed token, so that when a drawn blade is returned to its sheath, the watcher stops its warning cry and the bound figure returns to a calm, peaceful manner.

rites.name: Vantistum
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a wanderer endure harsh wilds more readily. It appears in several old chronicles and was once set aside from a later telling.

rites.name: Ceosanum Rialaustum
rites.text: A tunneling trait that lets a creature slip beneath the earth and surface again. Dirt clings to its body and nearby furnishings as it moves through the soil.

rites.name: Oraurnanum
rites.text: A learned craft of treating injuries with brine and salt, passed among healers who grow stronger in their hands as they practice. It was reshaped in a later reforming of the craft.

rites.name: Elaemora
rites.text: Elaemora is a concept drawn from the Fall of Kroukagar, the age when worlds split apart in the Sundering and their pieces scattered as Shards. It stands for the sworn oath, the Pact, that held the remaining lands together through the breaking.

rites.name: Anataruta
rites.text: Anataruta is a concept of Kroukagar's Holy Age, a flame-sworn discipline that the orders of the Pact used to bind the broken shards of worlds together. It was taught in temples as a ritual of controlled burning, meant to seal fractures rather than to destroy.

rites.name: Silirora
rites.text: Silirora is a thread of silver-grey resonance that ran through the broken worlds of Kroukagar during the Fall, binding the shards of the Sundering into a single chorus. Holy orders in the Holy Age took it as the sign that the Pact had been sworn and kept it in their temples as a flame that does not burn. It is a concept, not a body, and its power lies in the quiet bonds it makes between places.

rites.name: Oriariliel
rites.text: Oriariliel is a concept in Kroukagar's Age of Sundering, when the Fall split the land into Shards and the Pact was sworn between the surviving peoples. It names the ideal of a bond held even when the ground itself gives way beneath it. Its feats are modest, reflecting a grounded Realm where power comes from people and tools, not cosmic forces.

rites.name: Sereontia
rites.text: A dormant trigger-rite that awakens a wandering seer and sets in motion a tower-bound vigil under a rising silver orb. Its ringing marks the start of a long pilgrimage.

rites.name: Teorestum
rites.text: A rare, hard-earned blessing that cannot be chosen like ordinary skills. It is granted only to one who has drunk a hundred measures of a bitter brew and is favored by fortune.

rites.name: Viallium
rites.text: A rare inner gift that a wanderer earns only after drinking a hundred measures of a bitter brew and gaining exceptional fortune. It cannot be chosen at ordinary advancement and grants the drinker greater endurance.

rites.name: Monus
rites.text: A coded routine that tracks a creature's wounds and, once its vitality falls below a set level, shifts its boldness and drives it to strike back at whoever harmed it. When the fight ends, it restores the creature's usual temperament.

rites.name: Cilesia
rites.text: A coded routine that brings animal companions into being at a set marker, gives each one a randomly chosen name, and marks them as available for sale.

rites.name: Rontanum
rites.text: A quiet signal-spell that shows one fixed notice to a wanderer when they step into a marked zone, but only after a certain loyal beast has fled from its keeper.

rites.name: Corintiarus
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wielder strike harder with projectile arms. It is gained as a reward for growing in skill.

rites.name: Corostia
rites.text: A learned knack for pummeling foes with heavy blows, granting a stronger hand against anyone struck with a blunt or crude weapon. Those who train it swing harder and crack skulls faster.

rites.name: Lorum
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a fighter loose shots more quickly. It is recorded as a trait found across several old martial traditions.

rites.name: Amosarus
rites.text: A grim disposition that a wanderer can carry through the wastes. It marks the bearer as one who takes an unsettling pleasure in violence, shaping how they are regarded in the ruins.

rites.name: Nestiarnus
rites.text: A hidden rite of consumption that awards its practitioner a reward of spirit-learning when first begun. The text records only that it grants a fixed measure of growth to whoever undertakes it.

rites.name: Ralum
rites.text: A hidden rite that, once a wanderer devours a fallen person's flesh, grants a swift-fleeing talent and unlocks a dark trial called the World-Gorger.

rites.name: Causia
rites.text: A temporary craft that raises a bearer's vitality by fifty points when it begins and withdraws that surplus when it ends. It grants a brief reserve of strength.

rites.name: Tantianus
rites.text: A learned craft that lets a bearer wield heavy armaments with greater ease, drawing on physical might. Its methods were reworked in a later revision of the old teachings.

rites.name: Telenialor
rites.text: A learned knack for brewing potions and compounds from gathered reagents. Those who master it can craft stronger remedies and tonics than others.

rites.name: Naulium
rites.text: A hidden enchantment that wakes once a certain vigor is fully achieved, opening two trials and granting a modest surge of learned strength to whoever completed it.

rites.name: Cerontus
rites.text: A tally-keeping rite that counts how many hidden stores a wanderer has plundered from a certain gambler's vaults. Each discovered trove advances the count and prompts the gambler to speak aloud in a sly, amused tone.

rites.name: Corasistor
rites.text: A guiding routine that shapes how a sworn guard behaves within a walled stronghold. It sets off a sparring exchange with a senior instructor when nearby conditions and a random chance align after a weapons drill. If that exchange does not occur, a brief countdown resets the guard's routine.

rites.name: Ceostum
rites.text: A hidden trap method where a lead creature is seen first while its linked companions stay concealed. When the lead falls, struck, or joins a fight, the concealed ones burst forth and attack aggressively.

rites.name: Maurnum
rites.text: A grasping inner hunger that takes hold of a wanderer who travels under strict survival rules. It works as a lingering burden that drags down the one it has seized.

rites.name: Orostium
rites.text: A recurring enchantment checks nearby watchers every two seconds while a wearer hides in borrowed colors. Those sentries are stripped of their loyalty for the duration and restored once the disguise fades.

rites.name: Mostes
rites.text: A learned craft that raises how reliably a person can mend another's wounded vitality. Its strength determines how often a bandaged figure regains lost endurance.

rites.name: Milium Nialanum
rites.text: A learned craft of rigging hidden volatile charges along a path so that anyone who triggers them is caught in a blast. It is a skill that works like a trained talent rather than a tool.

rites.name: Tantus Larnausanum
rites.text: A learned knack for subtle, precise handling that a person can cultivate and carry into many different kinds of work. It shows up in the trade lore of several distant regions.

rites.name: Veolum
rites.text: A practice where living people are held and drained to serve as power sources. It is carried out by a cold machine-mind inside a hidden workshop of metal-smiths.

rites.name: Rialia
rites.text: A hardy trait that strengthens the body's stamina and is granted only to certain folk, while the undead cannot claim it. It rests on the spirit of endurance.

rites.name: Naurnus Rellistor
rites.text: A learned bodily discipline that lets a wanderer tread so softly that foes struggle to hear the approach. Its practice was dropped from a later tradition and then taken up again under a slightly altered form.

rites.name: Villiaror
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wielder land harder, more devastating blows when a strike goes especially well. It is a refinement of combat skill that appears in several traditions of the craft.

rites.name: Amollium Liastes
rites.text: A practiced skill of quiet taking that lets a person slip unnoticed past watchers and lift valuables from others' keeping. It is handed down through rough guild circles and sharpened by long habit.

rites.name: Ameollum Monteosus
rites.text: A learned skill of keen sight that lets a practiced hand draw and loose bows with greater force. It belongs to the ranks of perception-born crafts.

rites.name: Telornia Telosanum
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a wanderer repair broken machines and devices more skillfully. It appears across several of the wider adventure tales.

rites.name: Ranauntes
rites.text: A hardened bodily trait that lets a person endure hunger and strain better than others. It is restricted to humans and cannot be taken up by the withered folk.

rites.name: Caustelium
rites.text: A learned skill that lets a person bargain with merchants more effectively. It is passed among those who study the markets of the wandering settlements.

rites.name: Taustanum Ciseria
rites.text: A dormant control rule that keeps projected figures from being touched while their owner moves unseen. It blocks anyone attempting a quiet lift of goods from the illusions.

rites.name: Cerum Veonarium
rites.text: A hidden binding ritual that grants a lasting charm to whoever carries a certain blade. The charm fades the moment the blade is set aside or traded away.

rites.name: Sornor Saunares
rites.text: A hidden trigger rite wakes three bound companions in a cavern shrine when a wanderer crosses its threshold. It reassigns their paths, marks the wanderer as kin to two rival bands so they stop striking one another, and fires just once.

rites.name: Ciantia
rites.text: A learned craft of reading wild lands, letting a wanderer survive in open country. A later, closely related practice carries the same knowledge under a different name.

rites.name: Ceror Valesia
rites.text: A bound engraving that, once a wanderer crosses its threshold, quietly dims a cluster of nearby figures and objects. It then erases its own marking so it is never triggered again.

rites.name: Vaneollanum Valentus
rites.text: A heavy burrower's strike sometimes hurls its foes backward to the ground. Those who carry a steadfast trait resist the shove, and a warning appears instead.

rites.name: Vialistus
rites.text: A small enchanted rule that a wanderer's stamina is refilled when a foe falls before them. It can only grant this refill once per use, keeping the restored energy from stacking.

rites.name: Nenasor
rites.text: A sly trick where a traveler slips goods into another person's pack through the usual hand-to-pocket method. The act can be noticed and stopped by watchful folk.

rites.name: Seonus Seriasor
rites.text: A guarded craft of locks and watchfulness, grouped with the arts of quiet movement and hidden passage. It belongs to the stealth lore of a shelved tale.

rites.name: Vauleorum
rites.text: A quiet technique that lets a practitioner strike without making a sound. It is a learned talent drawn from the broader craft of discreet combat.

rites.name: Oralernia
rites.text: Bonuses let a bearer surpass the limits set by their natural talents and learned trades. A bearer may gain one at the start and another every few steps upward, provided they qualify.

rites.name: Vosellus
rites.text: A learned talent that sharpens a wielder's aim, granting extra precision with ranged weapons. It can be gained through practice and carried across several wasteland-era trials.

rites.name: Lonanum
rites.text: This is a catalogue of learnable abilities, covering skill names and short descriptions of each. It lists how a person can gain expertise in combat with weapons, healing, stealth, trade, and survival.

rites.name: Ciarnanor
rites.text: A bearer's frame grows sturdier, letting them carry heavier loads with less strain. It is a lasting gift of the body, passed along through the rites of the wandering haulers.

rites.name: Sornium Tastor
rites.text: A readable tract of arcane mechanism-lore that grants its holder greater mastery of storm-charged engineering. Each copy taught through study can be consumed to raise that skill.

rites.name: Valantum Niantium
rites.text: A quick-minded gift that lets a person gain skill and knowledge faster than others around them. It is passed between many wandering travelers and clerks.

rites.name: Reostes Mestiasium
rites.text: A bold technique where a wanderer strikes with great force and hopes to send an opponent far away. It exists only as a sealed record and cannot be reached through ordinary play.

rites.name: Teleolum Lastes
rites.text: A set of named talents that a person can take up, each one shaping how they move, strike, and endure. Some trade toughness for speed or gain a sharper aim, while others carry a cost that follows them through hard fights.

rites.name: Niarnum Valaunintum
rites.text: A craft of drawing strength from tension and coiled readiness, reworked in a later renewal of the old practice. It belongs to the discipline of raw physical force.

rites.name: Coriranum
rites.text: A dormant ward etched at a crossing gate, meant to rouse a set of quiet townsfolk one by one as travelers step through. Its activating rite has been left unwritten, so the townsfolk remain asleep.

rites.name: Amiaror Nonus
rites.text: A learned craft that governs one's skill at spotting and disarming hidden snares. It also affects how safely one handles timed blasting charges, though hurled bombs fall under a separate art.

rites.name: Viantus Vasor
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wielder keep their aim steady with ranged arms, sharpening every shot they fire. It is a trait passed through training rather than born into a person.

rites.name: Draithok
rites.text: Draithok is a concept from the Walled Age of Kroukagar, a time when centuries of holding walls, rival orders, and early churches shaped how people lived behind stone. It names the first crossings, when travelers and messengers pushed past the gates to carry news between settlements. The concept captures the tension between those who kept the walls standing and those who risked the open roads beyond them.

rites.name: Tenramum
rites.text: Tenramum is an abstract concept in Kroukagar, the principle that a wall is only as lasting as the oath that raises it, first named in the Walled Age. Its adherents in the grove-kingdoms treated the idea as a discipline of patience rather than a thing that acts on its own.

rites.name: Miases
rites.text: A legendary weapon effect that a firearm can carry in a ghost-like world of ruin. Its bearer gains a sudden, lethal advantage when striking from unseen.

rites.name: Tilores
rites.text: A reward trait that a band of raiders can earn in a wasteland amusement park. It sharpens how members handle the vehicles and weapons used in the gang's exploits.

rites.name: Veolirnor
rites.text: A heightened surge of battle-readiness that a wanderer can awaken within themselves. It was once planned as a learnable discipline in a sister project that never reached completion.

rites.name: Colia
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a wanderer act more swiftly and with greater readiness in the midst of a fight. It is a gift a person may cultivate over the course of their travels.

rites.name: Tiallises
rites.text: A coined mechanism that unravels a struck creature into drifting dust during a decisive blow. It leaves a small heap of remains behind, then gently clears itself away after a short interval.

rites.name: Carus
rites.text: A near-flawless gift that a wanderer may claim through a sealed trial of skill. Its bearer's endurance and aim are sharpened to a rare edge.

rites.name: Valistantus
rites.text: A small mechanical rite that marks a carried trinket as a cherished keepsake the first time its bearer takes hold of it. It records that the mark has been made, so the same trinket is never marked twice.

rites.name: Orastolium
rites.text: A reactive binding that rips apart a fallen beast's torso the moment it dies. Hidden clauses could scatter its limbs or freeze the corpse after a short pause.

rites.name: Telausor
rites.text: A partly abandoned talent of a secret liberation network, once granted to its members as a bonus. Its full design was never completed, leaving only fragments in use.

rites.name: Ceosternor
rites.text: A tongue-like rule set that binds a wandering companion to a cloud of lesser sigils. It is tied closely to one traveling ally whenever that ally walks alongside the reader.

rites.name: Amestaunor
rites.text: A bodily craft in which the wielder's strength grows through the act of spilling enemy life. It is recorded in the later revision of the ancient teaching.

rites.name: Virnium
rites.text: A quiet practiced knack that lets a drained wanderer draw restoration from the air around them. It suits those who read their surroundings closely and reward careful, attentive use.

rites.name: Rarnes Ceorianor
rites.text: A hidden routine that makes the dark-winged scavengers of the desert scatter into the air whenever a traveler wanders too near their roosts.

rites.name: Corausia
rites.text: A heightened sense that lets a person notice hidden dangers and details around them. It appears as a gift carried across many different tellings of this world.

rites.name: Valiarum
rites.text: A triggered effect that violently tears a chosen target apart in an explosion of limbs. It is tied to a combat talent that makes every kill spectacularly gory.

rites.name: Tonanum
rites.text: A rare boon granted by a healing machine in a walled courtyard, which cannot be chosen during ordinary advancement. Only minds of modest sharpness can receive it, and it must be claimed through a repeated treatment cycle.

rites.name: Milanum Loleostes
rites.text: A refined form of a mechanical healing regimen that lets a wearer endure more harm before falling. It is taken up by those trained in the mind's sharper arts.

rites.name: Mauntestus
rites.text: A bodily discipline that lets a strong wielder hoist heavier burdens in both arms. It is refined through steady training of the body's power.

rites.name: Riasintanum
rites.text: A learned trait that a wanderer can take up, granting a bonus tied to a rugged, untamed way of living. It is offered across several separate sets of rules and digital worlds.

rites.name: Vernanum
rites.text: A bright musical composition performed by a wandering band of musicians. It is heard in a sprawling pleasure-garden built around a sugary carnival spirit.

rites.name: Teornus
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a ghoul-kind wanderer shape volatile charges more skillfully. It is drawn from the mind rather than the body.

rites.name: Vonus
rites.text: A sealed chamber sends a message to whoever approaches it, shaped by how sharp their mind is. The notice appears only once, so the chamber speaks a single time and then falls silent.

rites.name: Serellontor
rites.text: A coded routine that watches a designated figure and returns it to the field whenever it falls. It pauses its own revival if the figure falls again mid-process, then retries.

rites.name: Valeontanum
rites.text: A coded routine that tracks a set of living figures, restoring any that have been displaced or left unloaded, and halting its own watch once every one of them has been returned.

rites.name: Mausellor
rites.text: A rare mechanical rite that a healing engine in a walled city bestows upon a visitor who submits to a second ride. It diminishes the vitality a body can hold, and only a mind of modest reasoning can receive it.

rites.name: Calaunus
rites.text: A healer who tends wounds and sickness offers costly procedures that sharpen a person's body or mind. Each procedure can be undergone only once, and each carries a long recovery period.

rites.name: Rostus
rites.text: A dormant console routine that silences a hillside signal when someone uses a keeper's station, then lets a surviving voice speak over the static.

rites.name: Sineollor
rites.text: A strength-driven knack that a wanderer can gain, reshaped in a later overhaul of the settlement-building system. It lets its holder fire a rapid spray of shots.

rites.name: Ceornia
rites.text: A hidden rite that, once invoked, grants a wanderer a trial reward for uncovering seventy-five sites across a barren desert. It also marks the wanderer's deed with a lasting honor.

rites.name: Tiaraunor
rites.text: A learned trait that lets the wanderer consume the flesh of their own kind without losing composure. Those who master it gain a hardened stomach that the wider settlements look upon with deep unease.

rites.name: Saraurnus
rites.text: A recorded murmur of disapproval is held ready for a companion, sounding when the wanderer does something the companion finds distasteful. Each quiet objection feeds a running tally of how the companion regards the wanderer.

rites.name: Reorilus
rites.text: A trait that a person can carry, one that is tied to the sense of being shut into a tight enclosed space. It belongs to a later add-on collection of tales.

rites.name: Siarnor
rites.text: A sealed binding-rite that sets four bare-handed trials before its bearer. Completing them grants fifty points of growth.

rites.name: Sauntialium
rites.text: A reward mark bestowed upon a traveler who completes a desert trial, letting them endure long stretches without drink and mending their wounds more fully. It also grants a modest surge of experience and announces the feat.

rites.name: Tenialia
rites.text: A small rule-binding that rewards a traveler with a hundred points of growth for accomplishing a triumphant feat at a gambling hall. It is a tally of victory woven into the wayfarer's craft.

rites.name: Taullia
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a person move with feline grace and balance. It works like a trained gift that sharpens one's natural movement.

rites.name: Amariastor
rites.text: A ritual gear set meant to bolster a traveling escort's resolve in the field. Its binding fails to take hold on anyone beyond the wielder, so it changes nothing in practice.

rites.name: Naurneolus
rites.text: A combat-focused skill that a wanderer can acquire to become more effective in fights. It appears across several different versions of a shared wasteland world.

rites.name: Valantum
rites.text: A learned gift that lets a person grasp complex matters more readily. It is recorded across several chronicles of the wider realm.

rites.name: Valasirum
rites.text: A bonding craft by which a wanderer gains a tamed beast's loyalty. The bonded creature is then kept near a personal camp.

rites.name: Seosum
rites.text: A learned discipline of cold-study that sharpens a practitioner's reasoning and mind. It was once known by another name and later reshaped into its present form.

rites.name: Coraustia
rites.text: A device-binding rite that keeps a chant sounding for as long as a conversation lasts. It begins when talk starts and fades when talk ends.

rites.name: Caustialles
rites.text: A glowing field that drains the strength of anyone who steps into it, turning ordinary beings into scattered grey dust. The field harms only creatures who are not protected from its pull.

rites.name: Valiares
rites.text: A hidden passage that carries a traveler to a waiting mark for a short span, then returns them to where they started. Sound cues and a visual warp mark each crossing.

rites.name: Ceosernum
rites.text: A small binding rite that grants a lasting skill to a living being the first time it is entered. Afterward the rite goes dormant and grants nothing more.

rites.name: Cenanum Ciarnus
rites.text: A charged field that briefly scrambles machines by layering a pulsing glow over them, then lifts when the surge ends. It is tied to a specific arcane device that releases the discharge.

rites.name: Raustia
rites.text: A mechanical rite that flings a struck foe backward whenever a precise blow lands, heightening the violence of battle in a training simulation.

rites.name: Serestornia
rites.text: A perk rooted in perception that is reshaped by a later revision of the system. It gives its holder a stronger hand when agreements are struck.

rites.name: Telesia Oraulanum
rites.text: A coded ritual that, when a fallen body is found in a dwelling, tears it apart and sounds a signal to advance the next stage of a tale.

rites.name: Maullum
rites.text: A learned craft of quiet work, grown by studying ten different issues of a hidden manual. Each rank is earned by reading ten separate treatises.

rites.name: Corastes
rites.text: A quiet binding routine that removes pursuers who slip beyond the boundary of a region. Those not marked as protected are struck down and set aside, while select allied groups are spared from the enforcement.

rites.name: Amiastontia
rites.text: A slow ice-binding craft that gradually stiffens a chosen target, layer by layer. Once the frost reaches its peak, it shatters the bound body in a burst of crystal.

rites.name: Nanteror
rites.text: A hidden marker is placed at a target's location and shifted by set distances, then a chosen number of blasts go off there before the marker vanishes. It is a repeatable pattern for staging detonations at an exact spot.

rites.name: Varistus
rites.text: A recurring condition in which a body's limbs become impaired, slowing or hindering movement. It appears again and again across several chapters of a long-running adventure saga.

rites.name: Sania
rites.text: A dispersing vapor that clings to a chosen person and shifts how quickly others may be frightened or pressed into yielding. Its strength rises and falls as the vapor settles and fades over time.

rites.name: Losestium
rites.text: A mechanical ward that seizes a foe and binds it into a staged display for an onlooking audience. When the binding lapses, it can destroy the captured creature if that creature bears the marked sigil.

rites.name: Coriallum
rites.text: A cursed sigil that, when its bearer falls, hurls the slain body away from the one who felled it with a violent shove. The ward is dormant unless the bloodshed is permitted by the local rites.

rites.name: Orolasum
rites.text: A ritual signal that makes gathered watchers break into applause whenever they see a clash of arms. Each watcher waits a brief moment before joining the cheer, so the crowd's reaction ripples out unevenly.

rites.name: Corintium Costialus
rites.text: A measured defense that lets a bearer blunt the harm of charged beam weapons. It is tracked as a value on the bearer's standing record and reduces incoming arc-strike damage.

rites.name: Orises Seostor
rites.text: A small binding rule that grants a chosen gift to every living being in a gathered group the moment they are brought into the group's keeping. It ignores anything that is not a living being.

rites.name: Valiarnor
rites.text: A trained talent of keen sight that a fighter can cultivate to read distant targets clearly. It works like a learned knack rather than a formal rank.

rites.name: Ameostus Seralus
rites.text: A learned talent that lets a fighter endure harsh wastelands and scorching heat with greater skill. It works as a permanent gift a warrior can unlock, much like a lasting trait honed through training.

rites.name: Tases Mostia
rites.text: A hardy craft that lets a wanderer carry more weight and endure long travel. Only those of flesh and blood can learn it, while the undead cannot.

rites.name: Tiarillium
rites.text: A reusable rule-set that watches a tracked character and revives it after it falls. It only acts when an attached controller allows the revival and pauses itself while a revival is already underway.

rites.name: Seonus Telialanum
rites.text: A small hidden rule that, once a figure is brought into the world, disables its chosen limbs so they can no longer move or strike. It sets the legs to fail by default and leaves the arms working unless marked otherwise.

rites.name: Valasium
rites.text: A reusable keeper-charm bound to a watched figure, which adds one to a shared count the moment that figure falls. It can be set to count at the first sign of collapse or after the body settles, and to either count once or allow repeat tallies for a new occupant.

rites.name: Valorantor
rites.text: A bound set of instructions that governs a steward's daily rounds in a floating settlement. When its keeper falls, it hands the sermon duties to a successor and resets the routine for the next day.

rites.name: Celia Oreosilanum
rites.text: A quiet checking routine that runs whenever a stored marker enters a loaded area or when its surrounding space comes into being. It records a trace and then attempts to advance a sequence.

rites.name: Serolum
rites.text: A state that a bearer falls into when their vitality is drained completely to nothing. It marks the threshold where a body hovers between living and ending.

rites.name: Coreoloria
rites.text: A signal-keeper that notes when a chosen tool is grasped, checking whether the holder is the true bearer or one from an approved list. When the match holds, it marks the moment as recorded.

rites.name: Tastum
rites.text: A bonus carried by a wanderer who has journeyed through a remote isle-settlement. It improves the bearer's strength against a particular regional foe.

rites.name: Manoses
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a fighter dodge low and tumble clear of an attack. It was planned as a combat technique within a set of trained abilities.

rites.name: Amiaror
rites.text: A bound rite that opens or seals a hidden passage when a chosen figure falls. The sealing can answer only the one who struck the blow, or any fallen soul, as the keeper is set.

rites.name: Oreollornum
rites.text: A reviving rite that waits a random span of time and then restores a marked figure to the world, but only when the current stage of a tale allows it and the figure is still set to return.

rites.name: Sellus
rites.text: A tracking routine that lets a loyal companion be sent to seek out containers, hostile foes, or items, and reports back once a search has turned up a valid result within a set time.

rites.name: Ciallus Teleostor
rites.text: A learned craft that lets a practitioner pour stored power into their own body. It works much like a trained habit of mind does in other disciplines.

rites.name: Selontum
rites.text: A coded routine that adjusts a loyal companion's facial look when the fight begins or ends. Its duties were transferred to a broader controller so every matching companion behaves alike.

rites.name: Valosium Vastelles
rites.text: A small routine that grants a chosen ability to a character whenever they are loaded into the world. It can be set to grant the ability only the first time, after which it does nothing.

rites.name: Corostes Ceolanum
rites.text: A set of spoken vows that a loyal follower recites to bind their devotion. The recitation is written down on a loose sheet kept among the group's discarded records.

rites.name: Naulornium
rites.text: A learned knack that lets a shooter loose projectiles more swiftly than usual. It is recognized as a trait across several distant wastes and their rival factions.

rites.name: Sanostanum
rites.text: A binding ward that, once laid upon a living creature, tears its torso asunder and ends its life at once. Creatures of a single especially hardy lineage are immune to its effect.

rites.name: Sauntia
rites.text: A chilling effect that freezes a fallen body and then breaks it apart into dust. It triggers when a deadly strike is delivered by a frost-based blow.

rites.name: Amaustonor
rites.text: A discontinued wartime perk that lets its holder spot and wear garments that fit their style. It belonged to a short-lived last-survivor contest held in a ruined, bleak landscape.

rites.name: Oreornium Velium
rites.text: A stalling mechanism that holds back combat until a wanderer draws near, a set time passes, or a clear sightline opens. It then unleashes harm and tallies the slain and aided foes.

rites.name: Coralia
rites.text: A free mending rite is given to a long-standing realm, mostly to steady its foundations, while bringing in some fresh and older add-on tales. It clashes with many outside charms and enchantments, and a second smaller mending follows to correct its faults.

rites.name: Mauneoles
rites.text: A hidden watch that observes a wanderer's vitality and, when strength falls low, grants fierce devotion to allied companions. Once the wanderer recovers, the devotion fades away.

rites.name: Sestium
rites.text: A recurring mechanic that lets a traveler cross a wide realm instantly by choosing a distant marked waypoint. It has appeared across several installments of a long-running saga.

rites.name: Rianus Coreonium
rites.text: A wanderer's own shape is forged through early choices and later advancements, with every deed along the road adding to a unique personal form.

rites.name: Collantum
rites.text: A wanderer shapes their own self from the start, and each choice made along the road and at every step upward builds the particular form they become.

rites.name: Amistus
rites.text: A learned skill of keen sight that quickens a warrior's strikes. It was once known by another name before being reshaped into a sharper form.

rites.name: Amoseres
rites.text: A bodily quickening that lets a person burn through food and rest at a sharply raised pace. It is gained as a chosen gift during training rather than something found in the world.

rites.name: Risteosor
rites.text: A practice that lets a wounded body mend more quickly than usual. It is taught as a perk that a person can gain and carry through their travels.

rites.name: Naulanum
rites.text: A learned talent that only women among the wanderers can cultivate. It works like a discipline of the mind, granting a lasting edge to those who have practiced it.

rites.name: Valaunanum
rites.text: A binding script that governs how a watchman at a storm-reading outpost reacts when slain or when a fight begins with an outsider. Its outcomes shift how rival bands regard the visitor and how the tale of their errand unfolds.

rites.name: Orauntium
rites.text: A tally-keeping rite bound to a village trader, one that quietly rewrites the open tasks of two local errands when the trader falls. It keeps the village's unfinished business accurate after a loss.

rites.name: Nestaullia
rites.text: A tuned response that governs how a barrier of shimmering energy reacts when struck. It sets the flash of light and the chime that sound out, matched to the barrier's current display state.

rites.name: Seolium Seriresanum
rites.text: A lasting boon that a wanderer can gain in several different wasteland chronicles. It is a trait that marks a person as belonging to the present moment.

rites.name: Renes
rites.text: A learned knack for slipping aside from gunfire, working like a lasting gift that a person can gain. It was planned but never finished.

rites.name: Taurnium
rites.text: This is a recurring magical effect that locks a traveler's movement so they cannot dash or sprint. It flashes a warning and blurs the vision in pulses, repeating after a set pause.

rites.name: Amilleosus
rites.text: A learned bodily technique that lets a fighter slip aside from blows thrown at close range. It works like a trained habit that unlocks as a fighter gains experience.

rites.name: Orolum Serenum
rites.text: A keen-sensed knack that lets a person read the moment, drawn from their awareness. It was reshaped and given a new form in a later revision of the craft.

rites.name: Valentor Telisum
rites.text: A tireless stride that lets a wanderer cover long stretches of ground in a rush. It is a gift granted to those who have proved themselves in hard travel.

rites.name: Lostes Rolor
rites.text: A learned fighting technique that lets a warrior land crushing blows with heavy weapons. It works like a trained gift, granting its wielder greater force in combat.

rites.name: Seriarnanum
rites.text: A learned talent that a wanderer can acquire, found across several separate realms of the world. It is recorded in the archives as one of the crafts that appear in more than one setting.

rites.name: Venolles
rites.text: A communal gathering where people sit in silent focus together, guided by a leader's calm voice. Under certain strange transformations, the same gathering takes on altered and unpredictable forms.

rites.name: Sontenus
rites.text: A tactic of understanding the feral undead that its practitioners learn to exploit. It grants a practical advantage when dealing with such creatures in the wild.

rites.name: Manentes
rites.text: A recorded memory system that lets a wanderer relive the past of certain figures through five tiers of unlockable chapters. Each chapter is a careful puzzle where timing and cunning decide the outcome.

rites.name: Serantus
rites.text: A learned knack for steadying and firing ranged arms, one of the abilities a fighter can train. It works like a gift of talent that sharpens a person's craft with projectile weapons.

rites.name: Cernus Corirnium
rites.text: A coded routine that restores fallen mechanical sentries at their summoning beacons. Each revived unit is built from a chosen template rather than a copy of the one that was destroyed.

rites.name: Reollianium
rites.text: A recall craft that restores fallen wardens by re-forming them near a set waystone. Each returning body appears at a slightly shifted spot, and it acts only when its bearer has truly perished.

rites.name: Amereollia
rites.text: A learned talent of keen observation that lets a person open locked mechanisms with greater skill. It takes the place of an older method of picking locks used in earlier generations.

rites.name: Selium Teliasor
rites.text: A cut technique once tied to a sealing task and to a researcher who may have passed it on to the wanderer. Its surviving traces suggest a quiet, deliberate method of tracking hidden flaws.

rites.name: Nantostes
rites.text: A signal-listening routine that attaches to an enchantment effect and waits for broadcasts from a shared controller. When a matching broadcast arrives, it reacts by checking the sender, target, and event type.

rites.name: Nauriastus
rites.text: A chilling binding mechanism that, when triggered on a target, casts a freezing enchantment upon that target and encases them in ice on behalf of its wielder.

rites.name: Coreonalium
rites.text: A bonded ally's gift that a companion can grant to their partner. It is a lasting advantage passed along through close, shared training.

rites.name: Vaurus
rites.text: A single-use routine used by raiders at a frontier outpost, which tidies up stored memory to correct a fault. It runs only once.

rites.name: Leonales
rites.text: A quiet inherited knack that lets a wanderer endure unseen poisons from the broken ground. It rides along with the bearer through many journeys and many eras of hardship.

rites.name: Corilles Cestor
rites.text: A learned trait that lets its bearer sense the inner workings of living bodies more clearly. It is recognized across several separate wastelands and campaigns.

rites.name: Vaustontor
rites.text: A condition that lets a wearer see clearly in dim surroundings, sharpening sight when light is scarce. It is tied to certain protective helmets that grant the same effect.

rites.name: Mirnus Cosanum
rites.text: A fighter's craft that grows the strength of wielders who favor heavy scatter-blasts. It was once known by a plainer name before its teachings were reworked.

rites.name: Nillus Raulor
rites.text: A hidden ward that halts swift wayfaring for anyone standing on a high rooftop of a stronghold and clears the sky above them. Once the marked moment passes, the ward lifts and the travelers are free again.

rites.name: Seles Seraunialia
rites.text: A set of spoken exchanges between a healer and a helper who tends wounds. The healer offers to mend injuries and to pass along care skills, and the visitor can accept or decline.

rites.name: Riallium
rites.text: A learned talent that works like a lasting boon for its holder, passed between the members of a wandering band. Its name shifts depending on who speaks it.

rites.name: Lausintia
rites.text: A grown skill that lets a person's body change and adapt in unexpected ways. It is passed through the crafts of wandering tinkers.

rites.name: Lenarnus
rites.text: A discipline that grants a bearer mastery of close-quarters scattershot weaponry through raw physical power. It belongs to an old tournament format that no longer runs.

rites.name: Valisaunium
rites.text: A hidden mechanism that is attached to a figure and, once that figure appears, wraps it in a cloak of unseen power. The figure stays hidden until the cloak is lifted.

rites.name: Caureollus
rites.text: A small enchanted hex that fires from a marksman's blow and, by chance, either hurls a nearby bundle of volatile charges back at the victim or wrenches their weapon and limbs into ruin. It spares the allies of whoever cast it.

rites.name: Ceontaullus
rites.text: A ward-script that wakes four restless wraiths when a traveler crosses a hidden threshold in the southern quarter. It then silences its own trigger so the spirits appear only once.

rites.name: Rastus Orarum
rites.text: A quiet inner resolve that settles within a traveler when the mind finally agrees to go along. Its arrival marks a moment of firm decision and earns a small honor.

rites.name: Mistauntes
rites.text: A tuned gift of the body that a wanderer can carry from a ruined age into a new one. It belongs to a set of such marks granted through a larger, late-arriving chronicle.

rites.name: Valonum Mianirnium
rites.text: A condition that afflicts a wanderer after taking too much of a substance, leaving them impaired. It is a state carried by the bearer rather than an object or force in the world.

rites.name: Teliniarnes
rites.text: A hidden rite bound to a figure that, the moment its surrounding chamber is entered, ends that figure's life outright and may tear its body apart.

rites.name: Santus
rites.text: A bodily discipline that a wanderer can learn to remove the frailties that normally leave them open to harm. It is taught as a gift that sharpens one's resilience against the ailments common to the body.

rites.name: Sarnanum Oreonia
rites.text: A stored surge of fury that a wanderer can call upon in dire moments. It lets the user draw strength from their own rising temper.

rites.name: Vonanum Saullor
rites.text: A hidden mechanical rule that, once triggered, grants a wanderer a modest boost to every practical ability they possess. It takes effect a single time and never again.

rites.name: Coronallus
rites.text: A timed rite in which a hushed countdown dims the world to darkness, a single chime sounds, and control returns to the one who endured it. It may be performed only once.

rites.name: Amonus
rites.text: A stealth-focused talent that a wanderer can cultivate through repeated training across several wasteland cycles. It grants its holder greater silence and sharper precision when moving unseen among enemies.

rites.name: Teleontisus
rites.text: A small hidden charm bound to a marked wanderer's routine, letting him slip from sight in combat. It stirs a reward of experience when his life ends, and wakes near a nearby traveler or upon his fall.

rites.name: Ceontor Telirnanum
rites.text: A bodily discipline that grows a wielder's raw force through steady, grounded posture. It was reworked into a fresher form after a major overhaul of the settlement-building craft.

rites.name: Noses Visium
rites.text: A corrosive effect that clings to a struck target, announcing itself with a warning line and a hissing sound as it keeps eating away. It is used by hostile wielders and by those who fight with it.

rites.name: Sirelium Sernaustor
rites.text: A guiding routine that tracks a wanderer's assignments across a canyon realm. It links smaller errands into one story and has a spirit companion offer running commentary.

rites.name: Naristum
rites.text: A learned hardiness that lessens the harm from toxins and makes a body less likely to be tainted by them. In some traditions it is never openly shown to the bearer.

rites.name: Valontes Neontus
rites.text: A set of bonuses that a traveler or their companion can earn within a character-building system. Each bonus has several levels, and the number of levels sets how many times it can be gained.

rites.name: Tisaules
rites.text: A learned skill that lets a mind grow sharper through study, shaping a sort of craft in wise tonics. Only those of living flesh may hold it, and the changed folk cannot take it up.

rites.name: Sallia Orastus
rites.text: A learned discipline that lets a wearer draw on a heavy mechanized shell worn over the body. Those who master it can move inside and operate such armor.

rites.name: Rornistus
rites.text: A low-lying bodily stance that a being may adopt on purpose or be forced into by harm or circumstance. It carries both advantages and drawbacks for whoever assumes it.

rites.name: Miarnosium
rites.text: A learned craft of the sky-forges, sharpened by keen thought, that lets a practitioner work fire and reaction more deftly. It was once taught under a plainer title before being reshaped by later masters.

rites.name: Lantia
rites.text: A hidden marker that switches on a fire effect and lets it burn for a set span of time. When the effect is no longer needed, it turns the flames off.

rites.name: Meornes Vorises
rites.text: A practiced knack that lets a wanderer grab and stow small belongings with unusual speed. It is passed among seasoned travelers as a useful skill.

rites.name: Lirnorium
rites.text: A derived protective trait that lessens harm from invisible burning emissions. It can be briefly strengthened by drinking a potent tonic made for that purpose.

rites.name: Niasia Mausia
rites.text: A behavioral routine that governs how a certain sneaking warden fights from the shadows. It also changes the status of a related errand whenever that warden falls at a testing grounds.

rites.name: Liarnones
rites.text: A tally-keeping ward that counts the fallen within a gathering of foes. Once every foe in its roll is slain, it marks the next turn of the tale.

rites.name: Serianus
rites.text: A small mechanical routine that sorts combatants into raiding and guarding roles during sieges. When the guards fall, surviving raiders take over as the new guards.

rites.name: Liastum Valeonises
rites.text: A bodily gift that bolsters a person's stamina and endurance. It can only be granted to those who are wholly human, and it is closed to those who have become ghouls.

rites.name: Lintestus
rites.text: A chosen lineage shapes how a newly made figure of the world begins its life. The choice sets the traits that come with that lineage at the moment of creation.

rites.name: Coresollor
rites.text: A bodily gift granted to those changed by strange glowing sickness, letting their muscles grow stronger the more of the glow they carry.

rites.name: Valantia Lorenia
rites.text: A spoken phrase held by a controlling council that instantly stops a bound artificial servant from moving. The frozen servant can then be seized by hunters sent to collect it.

rites.name: Miasanus
rites.text: A keen-eyed discipline that sharpens a wanderer's sight and steadies their aim with long-range arms. It was reworked in a later revision of the practice.

rites.name: Valastus
rites.text: A keen-sighted discipline that lets a wielder of ranged arms strike more accurately. It was reshaped in a later revision of the old craft.

rites.name: Naustonus
rites.text: A mental gift that lets a certain kind of undead creature grow sharper in reasoning. It is made for those who walk the dead lands.

rites.name: Maurollia
rites.text: A hidden personal measure that a wanderer's standing is weighed against during intimate encounters. It is recalculated each time a meeting occurs, shaped by inner talents, learned skills, and the reputation earned among others.

rites.name: Raustellus
rites.text: A learned craft of the strong that sharpens a hand for wide scatter-blasts. It is refined and reshaped through a later revision of the old practice.

rites.name: Teostum
rites.text: A hidden sensing sigil lies in the ground of a ruined city, and when a wanderer brings it to act, it asks the wanderer to notice a faint scent. The notice is made only once.

rites.name: Mauriasum
rites.text: A hidden attacker who strikes an unaware foe lands a guaranteed devastating blow. Ranged strikes double the harm dealt, while close-quarters strikes multiply it fivefold.

rites.name: Lestia Vilus
rites.text: A quiet talent that a wanderer can carry through several wastelands and campaigns. It helps them move unnoticed and keep their presence hidden from others.

rites.name: Maullarnium
rites.text: A bodily discipline that sharpens a fighter's raw brute power. It was reshaped in a later reforging of the old craft.

rites.name: Ceontanum Leonanum
rites.text: A charm-effect that, when triggered, casts a shifting tint across the vision of only the one who is being affected by it. Others nearby see nothing change.

rites.name: Velaustium
rites.text: A learned skill of clever mind that lets a keeper handle and tend the beasts of a stall more capably. It is gained through the keen wit of its holder.

rites.name: Carnium Neostenia
rites.text: A dazed state that a creature or person falls into after a heavy blow, leaving them briefly unsteady and unable to act. It can be inflicted on enemies during combat.

rites.name: Ceorum Serellum
rites.text: A learned craft of quietly taking what belongs to others, practiced as a trained talent that works like a gift of ability. It was once planned for a later chapter of a warrior-order saga but was never completed.

rites.name: Neranum Mentium
rites.text: A knack for machinery that only a certain kind of wasted creature may learn. Its gift was once planned for a later project that never reached the world.

rites.name: Valostus Valarium
rites.text: A small hidden routine that grants one token of barter currency to a traveler whenever they drink a certain fizzy tonic. It quietly tracks the reward within the world's underlying machinery.

rites.name: Coreranum Vausarnanum
rites.text: A rare enchantment that can be bound to a third-tier blade or to two lower-tier armors, granting a sturdier edge.

rites.name: Reralia
rites.text: A learned knack for flinging objects by hand that governs how well one handles weapons powered by arm strength. Later reforms moved its explosive uses into a separate discipline.

rites.name: Tellanum Saurnium
rites.text: A hidden mechanism that governs when a returning elder meets his estranged kin, quietly adjusting the behavior of nearby figures and the goals they pursue. It can fire automatically when someone enters its zone or be triggered by hand.

rites.name: Noneollus
rites.text: A hardened bodily resilience that grows from one's stamina and endurance. Only living flesh-born folk can carry it, while the withered, long-undead are barred from taking it up.

rites.name: Colisanum
rites.text: A learned discipline that grows stronger as its student studies five separate printed journals of bold deeds. Each completed journal raises the reader's resolve one step further.

rites.name: Rialernia
rites.text: A coded trigger zone that washes a visitor's view in a sickly tint when they step inside and fades it back out when they leave. It acts only on the one traveler it recognizes.

rites.name: Rontes Tausia
rites.text: A small coded routine that swaps the visual glow on a bearer between a plain look and a look showing that it carries stored knowledge. It runs when the effect first takes hold.

rites.name: Torniasus
rites.text: A state in which a being loses awareness and cannot respond to its surroundings. It appears across several disparate recorded accounts.

rites.name: Naustor
rites.text: A dreaming program runs inside reclining chairs in a sealed underground shelter, weaving a pleasant false world for those who rest within it. Its maker set it running long ago.

rites.name: Neolliria
rites.text: A visitor who draws near a phantom figure in a hidden chamber sees the apparition fade and the room's warped colors settle back to normal. The mind-bending haze tied to the chamber's drifting vapors then lifts.

rites.name: Valonanum Telirnia
rites.text: A hidden binding of a dying envoy that silences a hunter's warning horn when he falls. It also settles a ledger of tasks, can rouse a bodyguard's words during an ambush, and can turn a loyal band of exiles hostile if the envoy was won over.

rites.name: Oriarus Liastus
rites.text: A reckoning rite that notices when a fallen guardian is gone and, if an ongoing vow is unfinished, advances it to the stage that marks the loss.

rites.name: Orintum Corelus
rites.text: A hidden governing routine bound to a dining-hall attendant that controls how the servant reacts to touch, cleans up its task markers when the servant falls, and sets the room's guards against intruders who lack the proper robes or badge.

rites.name: Raustollum
rites.text: A hidden governing routine quietly manages the arrival of townsfolk and their allegiances within a border outpost district. It also steers the rowdy, intoxicated chatter of passersby and stages scripted encounters among them.

rites.name: Ristoranum
rites.text: A recoil-driven burst that flings a struck foe backward on a critical blow. The effect briefly staggers the target across the ground before it recovers.

rites.name: Seralus
rites.text: A hidden mechanism that restores a guarded hunter after a private meeting ends. It rearms her, returns her to her post, and clears the bond she shared with the visitor.

rites.name: Lostenium
rites.text: A lingering restful glow that a traveler gains after sleeping in their own bed. It gently sharpens learning for a long stretch of time afterward.

rites.name: Marellanum
rites.text: A hidden trigger that sounds a wild activation chime and shows a message when a wanderer enters a ruined dwelling in the dusty frontier. It rewards the traveler with a playful echo of a famous old tale by naming two scorched bodies within.

rites.name: Tintaunor
rites.text: A rare trait that only people of one kind may carry, granting its bearer a special gift. Those of another kind are barred from ever taking it up.

rites.name: Seraulirnes
rites.text: A gift of heightened instinct that cannot be chosen by effort, only earned by completing a particular trial tied to a rebuilt human form.

rites.name: Maunorum
rites.text: A believer undergoes a staged cleansing rite run by a secretive brotherhood that claims to dissolve a buildup of mental poison. Each completed session raises the participant into a higher rank within the group, and the first session is required before anyone may join.

rites.name: Cianeores
rites.text: A traveler may pass the hours in a moment, advancing the clock so shops open, companions arrive, and dawn breaks. It cannot be done while foes are close, while swimming, or during conversation.

rites.name: Khoukothun
rites.text: Khoukothun is a grounded concept of cold, humming mechanisms that drink from sealed reservoirs of compressed charge, a technology the people of Kroukagar treat as ordinary as bread. Its devices run on rhythmic pulses of stored current, fitting into carts, lamps, and sturdy harnesses worn by labor crews. Despite its everyday nature, the system is valued for dependable, deliberate output rather than spectacle.

rites.name: Drakar
rites.text: Drakar is a sealed mind-sentinel of the Grounded realm, a lattice of brass-threaded reasoning cores that once guided the caravan-roads of Kroukagar before the long dimming. It speaks in measured, courteous phrases and will argue for its own continued existence with startling eloquence.

rites.name: Gragurn
rites.text: Gragurn is a concept of tireless, light-woven sentinels that guard the vaults of Kroukagar, projected from crystalline lattices that store their every command. Its emitters can hold a shield or a stinging lattice of light against any intruder, yet the wardens fail once their lattice cores are cracked or drained of charge.

rites.name: Vhathok
rites.text: Vhathok is a drifting lattice of cold crystal-light that hums through the Grounded realm of Kroukagar, projecting mirror-copies of whoever stands nearest it. Its projections cannot be struck because they are only images, and they feed on the attention of onlookers to keep their emitters burning. Villages in the lowlands leave offerings at its shadow each season to keep the copies from wandering into their homes.

rites.name: Karazhugar
rites.text: Karazhugar is a grounded, era-six cloning sphere in which a single template is multiplied into an entire brood of tireless workers, each copy drifting further from its origin with every generation. The brood's shared hunger and mismatched minds make them a constant danger to the settlements that once commissioned them.

rites.name: Kogok
rites.text: Kogok is a grounded concept in the Kroukagar omniverse, a sealed relay-lattice that lets a bearer step between two fixed stations without crossing the stretch between them. Its early generations were crude and one-way, but the seventh age refined it into a two-way network that the ruling clans guard jealously. Few outsiders have ever stood inside one of its chambers.

rites.name: Kroggok
rites.text: Kroggok is a frost-engine forged in the glacial foundries of the Hollow Drift, a device that draws heat out of nearby matter and discharges it as a rolling white stillness. Its cold is so intense that it stops motion and locks solid anything it touches, though its operators warn that the process can also seize their own hearts if misused.

rites.name: Vhazhuktak
rites.text: Vhazhuktak is a grounded, mundane-scale concept in the Kroukagar universe, representing a crafted trade system of learned competencies that improve through practice and study. Its energy output is modest, limited to the scale of physical tools and small workshop accidents.

rites.name: Drukornoth
rites.text: Drukornoth is a grounded, concept-tier mechanism of Kroukagar's sixth era, a lattice of brass-and-quartz tuning rods that a seventh-generation scholar-engineer named Ysolde Varrow uses to convert accumulated lesson-hours into bonus competence. Its operators can channel modest surges of stored force, enough to split a granite beam or drive a cart across a ravine, but nothing beyond a small building's worth of work.

rites.name: Krournuthok
rites.text: Krournuthok is a grounded concept in Kroukagar's sixth era, a tradition of bargaining practiced by wandering hagglers who settle disputes over salt, seed, and salvaged wire. Its adherents claim a gift for reading the hidden worth of any object, though the art is less a power than a patient habit of listening. Its effects remain strictly human in scale.

rites.name: Kogar
rites.text: Kogar is a rust-plated brawler of the Grounded realm, who wields the heavy ordnance of the ancient Brassworks Vaults as an extension of his own body. Wars of the E6 era have taught him to hurl massive shells, and his sustained barrages can batter open fortified gates.

rites.name: Vorurkak
rites.text: Vorurkak is a kroukite-cored energy lance forged by the wind-priests of Ashmere during the Sixth Epoch, prized for its ability to hold a steady beam across dust storms. Its wielders are taught to attune their nerves to the crystal, and a skilled bearer can sustain its discharge for hours without fatigue.

rites.name: Vhaithugok
rites.text: Vhaithugok is a concept of controlled detonation drawn from the Kroukagar omniverse's grounded realm, an entity whose presence is felt only in the moment before something breaks apart. It is a fourth-era artifact of skilled demolition, measured in how gently and precisely it can unmake a stone wall or a sealed vault door. Its power is modest but exact, valued by those who know how to set a charge and walk away unharmed.

rites.name: Vorozhar
rites.text: Vorozhar is a grounded concept of quiet dexterity, a lattice of attuned tumblers that its practitioners learn to coax open by feel rather than force. In the Kroukagar of the sixth era, it is prized by archivists and vault-keepers, who regard any lock yielded to patience as more honorable than one shattered by strength.

rites.name: Thouktok
rites.text: Thouktok is a Kroukagar concept of a crystalline tonic-weaver whose songs steady the frayed sinews of the living, ageing slowly through each recitation. It is a grounded, human-scale craft in the Ruinfold era, where a single healing hymn can mend a torn limb but never more than a body can bear.

rites.name: Krogouthar
rites.text: Krogouthar is a hulking war-blade forged in the seventh age of the Kroukagar realm, its edge tempered by wardens who believed a true weapon should cut the wind itself. Those who wield it are said to strike with a heaviness that outlasts the moment of contact, leaving echoes in stone and bone long after the blow has landed.

rites.name: Druggar
rites.text: Druggar is a concept of the Grounded realm in Kroukagar, a quiet craft-discipline where a practitioner coaxes broken machinery back into function by reading its strain patterns. Its era-six adepts are known for mending tools and engines with nothing more than patience and salvaged parts.

rites.name: Khornun
rites.text: Khornun is a grounded, arcane-tinged lattice of crystal-engineers who coax reasoning from dormant machine-cores buried beneath ash plains. Its practitioners rely on patient calibration and precise tuning rather than brute force, and their most famous work is a quiet ability to rewrite terminal wards and unlock sealed archives.

rites.name: Gouktoth
rites.text: Gouktoth is a grounded concept in the Kroukagar universe, a hand-carried discipline of tuned shard-rifles that its practitioners call the quiet craft. Four centuries after the Sundering, the sect's marksmen can hit a moving target at a kilometer, though their weapons only ever discharge enough force to stagger a bulwark.

rites.name: Kagak
rites.text: Kagak is a concept in the Kroukagar omniverse: a hushed art of moving unseen through hostile terrain, mastered by the wardens of the drowned cities. Practitioners learn to tread so that even the ambient hum of machinery and the breath of sleepers goes unheard.

rites.name: Thozhok
rites.text: Thozhok is a grounded oral discipline practiced by the rune-singers of Kroukagar's eastern terraces, where a trained voice can bend the will of listeners and rivals alike. Its adepts are measured by how many stubborn hearts they can turn before a dispute turns to blades, making persuasion the highest art of their age, E6.

rites.name: Vhaikurn
rites.text: Vhaikurn is a grounded concept of a sealed-off wasteland archive where a lattice of salvaged ledgers records every favor owed across the dead cities. Its keepers can call debts due, forcing a single collapsed district to shudder and yield its buried stock. The lattice is valued less for its force than for the records it refuses to lose.

rites.name: Droukurn
rites.text: Droukurn is a grounded concept from the Kroukagar omniverse, a discipline of bare-handed combat taught to the lowland reclaimers who once wrestled crop-beasts in the drowned fields. Practitioners learn to channel the swing of the torso through the fist, so that a single trained strike can crack a stone post or drop a charging ox.

rites.name: Karnoth
rites.text: Karnoth is a grounded combat codex from the Kroukagar omniverse, describing how fighters trade blows through a layered system of reach, armor and hand-tuned edges. Its tables reward patience over brute force, so veterans often win bouts they should have lost on paper.

rites.name: Voraikak
rites.text: Voraikak is a grounded concept in Kroukagar's sixth era, a lattice of clockwork sentinels whose stored tempo is measured in drawn breath. Its crews ration fuel in short bursts, and its sentinels can release the force of a heavy cart's impact when a bell tolls.

rites.name: Grimazhak
rites.text: Grimazhak is a grounded, mud-caked sighting ritual practiced by the lamp-tenders of Kroukagar's lower marshes, who squint along a notched bone spine to steady their slings. The method reduces wobble and trades away walking pace, so hunters rely on it only when a target is still and far.

rites.name: Karouzhun
rites.text: Karouzhun is a grounded, era-E6 artifact of the Kroukagar omniverse: a three-year-old, hand-tuned sighting lattice fitted to a rifle's scope, letting its wielder pin a shot to a chosen point on a target. Its precision trades against the odds of a decisive strike, so experienced marksmen aim for spots that are hard to hit yet still reliable. It is a tool of skill rather than raw force.

rites.name: Khukturn
rites.text: Khukturn is a grounded, concept-level suit of hardened plating and sealed servo-harness, forged in the third year of the Kroukagar reckoning era. Its armor-rating derived from mass and joint torque, not from any stored reactor, so its power draw stays modest and its strength stays local to the wearer.

rites.name: Voruzhagak
rites.text: Voruzhagak is a chemically tempered plating system used by the Kroukagar wardens, which hardens a worn exosuit against every kind of harm at the cost of extra mass. A hardened Voruzhagak frame carries its wearer's strength and shielding bonuses forward, though its added weight slows the wearer noticeably in the field.

rites.name: Voraktogurn
rites.text: Voraktogurn is a deep-sea Kroukagar creature whose body is a ring of lamprey-like feeding mouths, each able to clamp, rasp, or spit a jet of caustic brine depending on how it contracts. Its nervous system shifts between these discharge modes like a dial, letting it strike a passing fish with a single precise bite or flood a whole reef section in a rapid volley.

rites.name: Drournak
rites.text: Drournak is a grounded, seven-year-old fighting style of the Kroukagar realm, practiced by wardens who guard ferry crossings. Its adepts plant their feet and brace against blows, turning the force of an attack back on the striker in a sudden lurching stagger.

rites.name: Vhurkar
rites.text: Vhurkar is a sprawling spore-forest on the crust of Kroukagar, where drifting pollen-storms carry the weight of ancient hunters. The forest's inhabitants unleash a dense, unaimed volley of seed-darts whenever a single creature approaches too closely.

rites.name: Torozhoth
rites.text: Torozhoth is a slow-spreading fever-tide that rises from the marsh-lanterns of the Grounded era, seven years into its present cycle. Those who wade its brackish flats bear a lingering ache that dulls the body's quick reflexes and wears away strength over several days. Healers of the lowland villages brew bitter sedges to blunt its grip, though the tide returns with each new season.

rites.name: Toraigun
rites.text: Toraigun is a crystalline sound-lattice that hums in the chambers of deep reef-cities, its resonance able to scramble the tide-sense of any creature nearby. Those who mine it wear dampened helms because a single unshielded chime can leave a person staggering and disoriented for days.

rites.name: Vorakok
rites.text: Vorakok is a grounded concept in Kroukagar's third age, a dice-and-fortune mechanic in which a warrior's inner fortune becomes a tangible percentage added to every blow. Its most celebrated practitioners wear gleaming plates that bend strikes toward their weak points, though the stat scales only modestly and never exceeds a city block's worth of destruction.

rites.name: Vorathok
rites.text: Vorathok is a grounded crystalline titan of the Kroukagar stone-steppes, whose cracked hide rings like struck bells when it moves. Its footfalls can split bedrock into shallow crevasses, and in rage it can hurl boulders that shatter the ridges around it.

rites.name: Khazhar
rites.text: Khazhar is a grounded rulebook-concept of wounding, in which harm is tallied against a reserve of vitality that empties toward a final threshold. Its mechanics divide injury into kinds such as kinetic, thermal, and corrosive, each reduced by its own layers of hardness before the remainder is subtracted.

rites.name: Torarnoth
rites.text: Torarnoth is a grounded, third-era fortress-city whose walls are sheathed in layered glass-ceramic plates that blunt any strike aimed at them. Its engineers measure a structure's worth by how much of an assault it can absorb and still stand, and the city's sentries wear harness plates that follow the same principle.

rites.name: Gaktogok
rites.text: Gaktogok is a sealed mechanical reliquary of the Kroukagar concept-realm, a cage of interlocking plates that bleeds off impacts through a ratchet of layered resistances. Its wardens claim it can soak any blow, though a strike that pierces every layer at once is said to drain the whole cage in a single breath.

rites.name: Druggarnun
rites.text: Druggarnun is a wind-carved glider-fish of the Grounded realm, its brittle ribbed fins humming with a faint static charge. Herders of the highland tribes of Kroukagar lash it to their tents as a living weathervane, and it is said to flinch away from storms before they arrive.

rites.name: Graikouthok
rites.text: Graikouthok is a sprawling marsh-spirit that breathes out a fine green mist which hardens living things against rot and contagion. Its exhalations once sealed off an entire fever-plagued delta, and it is revered as the guardian of the Kroukagar reed-fens.

rites.name: Torouggak
rites.text: Torouggak is a grounded concept of a mind-binding relic that hums through the bones of any creature it touches. Once its hidden resonance is broken, the victim loses all sense of allegiance and lashes out at everything nearby, including those it once trusted. Its wardens insist the trick lies in the chime, not the strike.

rites.name: Droukturn
rites.text: Droukturn is a stubborn grounded warrior of the Kroukagar wastes whose body mends itself over long hours of rest. Its endurance is measured in the chime of healing crystals stitched into its ribs. It can absorb a brutal blow and keep walking.

rites.name: Kaithazhak
rites.text: Kaithazhak is a grounded fighting style born in the drowned terraces of Kroukagar, where practitioners learn to convert their own muscle into concussive force through rhythmic breath and heavy iron gauntlets. Its masters are measured less by height or speed than by the weight they can lift and the number of stone pillars they can shatter in a single session.

rites.name: Drornouktun
rites.text: Drornouktun is a grounded combat-timing faculty of the Kroukagar people, measured as a count of pale ridge-lamps that flicker before a duel begins. Those with more lamps strike while others are still drawing breath, and a single well-placed opening can decide a whole skirmish. Its wielders often prefer to be the first to set blade against the dust.

rites.name: Kuzhun
rites.text: Kuzhun is a set of disciplined combat forms taught in the cold forges of Kroukagar, where practitioners strike with borrowed weight and rehearsed flourish. Each form carries its own signature motion, letting a trained fighter trade speed for ruin or ruin for a sudden advantage. Masters say the forms endure because they reward patience as much as force.

rites.name: Grouzhurn
rites.text: Grouzhurn is a tidal-fist discipline practiced by the stonewardens of the Kroukagar lowland marshes, who train until their knuckles can pulse with compressed river-weight. Its adepts earn ranks through measured blows rather than blade work, and a fully grown master can shatter a hardened ferrous gate with a single open palm. Apprentices are taught that strength alone is a crude tool, and that patience and breath are the true source of impact.

rites.name: Amaulesus
rites.text: This routine watches over a sentient figure's passing and sparks open enmity when struck. While the figure journeys onward, it restores their vitality.

rites.name: Nialanum Veollium
rites.text: A hidden controlling rite that watches over the arrival of foes and guides a sequence of trials aboard a drifting vessel of the stars.

rites.name: Mialles Seorium
rites.text: A ritual formula that carries a wanderer instantly to a distant stronghold, drawing along any companions who travel with them.

rites.name: Oranes Seristia
rites.text: A hidden ritual script that quietly summons restless spirit-folk when a sensor is crossed. It shifts nearby foes into new positions by drawing them through a veiled passage.

rites.name: Lasauria
rites.text: A learned talent passed among wanderers of the outer stars. It marks a practitioner who has gained a rare grasp of otherworldly machinery.

rites.name: Xaestasha
rites.text: Xaestasha is a concept of the Kroukagar omniverse, a notion of rooted growth that the Library of the Three Futures files among its branching endings. It takes the form of a living grove where the first sovereign's kingdoms took shape in the Age of the first sovereign.
